newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris to challenge Florida ruling.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris to challenge Florida ruling.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said Wednesday it would challenge a Florida appeals court ruling allowing the state to use internal tobacco company documents as evidence in its lawsuit against the cigarette makers.
"This ruling, plainly and simply, is wrong," said Gregory Little, senior assistant general counsel for Philip Morris, "and we intend to challenge it, or appeal immediately."
In West Palm Beach on Wednesday, Florida's 4th District Court of Appeal upheld a ruling allowing the state to use as evidence 13 documents obtained from Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group.
Florida sued the tobacco companies to recoup the public cost of treating smoking related illness. Jury selection is scheduled to begin in the trial on Aug. 1.
The Liggett documents include memos on trial strategy, a 1964 consumer survey, a 1966 letter on the status of special company projects and a 1978 letter about carbon monoxide analysis.

The tobacco companies had argued that the documents were protected by attorney-client privilege. But the appeals court found the documents exempt because they involved alleged plans to commit a crime or fraud. ((--Miami Bureau, 305-374-5013))
